1.why: All nine screens show a static, uncluttered card layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Bold headings and high-contrast blue primary buttons make the main actions and titles clearly stand out on every page.

3.why: Each screen is narrowly focused on one task with a single prominent form, though the long multi-step sequence itself may slow finding the end goal.

4.why: The flow requires remembering and entering a recovery token, two separate MFA codes, and complex password rules across many distinct steps.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill affordances, or “remember me” controls appear on the password or sign-in screens.

6.why: No previously saved credentials, familiar devices, or recognizable account cues are displayed for the user to recognize.

7.why: Labels and instructional sentences are consistently short, plain-language, and easy to read on every step.

8.why: None of the screenshots show any error messages, so the system does not demonstrate descriptive error text or recovery guidance.

9.why: An explicit format example is given for the account-contact field and password-composition rules are listed beneath the new-password inputs.

10.why: Only password-plus-code entry is offered; no alternative choices such as face login or other authenticators are presented.

11.why: Each individual screen presents essentially one primary action and at most a single secondary link, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Success outcomes are explicitly confirmed (e.g., “recovery instructions have been prepared”, “Privacy statement accepted”).

13.why: Contextual tips appear on most steps (token lifetime, password rules, safe-authentication reminders).

14.why: No dedicated “try again” or back buttons are visible, although blank form fields could in principle be re-filled.

15.why: Header, card layout, button style, typography and safety-note placement remain identical across all nine steps.
